checked.note: verified in a running system - human live check 2026-08-02 (maintainer): app started and exercised, no findings.

deviations.what: sap.m.Dialog.showFullScreenButton is @since 1.149 - it is the very property this sample demonstrates, so dropping it would drop the sample. Kept 1:1 (fidelity-first, the corpus-wide POST_171 policy); the app needs UI5 >= 1.149 to show the toggle, everything else renders on 1.71.

the original builds its three Dialogs imperatively in the controller (new Dialog({...}).open(), each cached in a controller field and added as a view dependent); the port expresses each as a core:FragmentDefinition popup shown via client->popup_display on the button press (app 019/273 precedent). Every fragment control is therefore EXTRA vs the archived V.view.xml, which holds only the three trigger Buttons: Dialog, List, StandardListItem and the dialog's own OK/Close Buttons (Button 3 -> 5, Dialog/List/StandardListItem 0 -> 1 per open dialog).

the three dialogs differ only in resizable / draggable / the fixed contentWidth+contentHeight and in the first one's extra Emphasized OK begin button, so the port builds them through one popup_products_display( resizable draggable sized begin_ok ) method. Each flag is written ONLY when the original passes it - the plain dialog gets no resizable='false' and no contentWidth, so no attribute the original never sets is added.

the List binds the shared demo mock products.json /ProductCollection (all 123 rows, Name + Quantity - the only two fields the StandardListItem binds) inlined into model_init; the original loads the same file through a JSONModel. Both dialog buttons (OK and Close) close the dialog client-side via follow_up_action( cs_event-popup_close ), the direct form of the original's this.oDialog.close().

**e2e-verified 2026-08-01** (scripts/e2e-smoke.mjs interaction, transpiled backend + real browser): the plain dialog opens with its title 'Available Products' and the bound 123-row product list inside it, and the Close button closes it client-side (popup_close). Residual (nothing headless can assert): the fullscreen toggle itself - corrected 2026-08-23, the stated reason was wrong. The harness does NOT serve an old runtime: e2e-smoke resolves every sdk.openui5.org request to the installed @openui5 packages, pinned at 1.151, so showFullScreenButton is live headless and Dialog._applyFullscreenButtonToHeader really does add the button (this port sets no customHeader and the context is not a phone). The module already opens that dialog, so the button's presence, its tooltip swap and the stretched dialog are all assertable - the leg is open for want of an assertion, not for want of a runtime and the resizable/draggable behaviour of the other two dialogs, which differ only in the flags the same builder writes.
